training-serving-skew.name: Training-serving skew
training-serving-skew.definition: A mismatch between computations or data used in training and serving.
training-serving-skew.explanation: A model trained on standardized inputs expects the same mean, scale, feature order, and missing-value policy during inference. Recreating preprocessing from memory can silently shift every score while the weight file still loads. The project stores preprocessing values beside the model and validates the input schema before prediction. Versioning this bundle makes the dependency explicit. It does not detect every semantic change in upstream data, so monitoring remains necessary.

model-artifact.name: Model artifact
model-artifact.definition: A stored, versioned package of inference state and metadata.
model-artifact.explanation: The miniature artifact contains a format version, model version, input schema version, preprocessing statistics, learned parameters, and a training-data fingerprint. Loading checks the exact field count, supported versions, positive scale, and finite numbers. A production artifact may also contain architecture, labels, tokenizer files, dependency versions, signatures, and provenance. A filename alone is not a sufficient contract because it cannot prove that the bytes and the serving schema agree.

data-drift.name: Data drift
data-drift.definition: A change in the distribution of inputs observed over time.
data-drift.explanation: The project compares a live request mean with the training mean and triggers a threshold alert. This is a simple observable signal, not proof that accuracy declined: harmless seasonality can move inputs, and unchanged averages can hide important shifts. Useful monitoring names the reference window, statistic, segment, sample count, and action threshold, then connects drift signals to delayed labels and service health when those are available.

rollback.name: Rollback
rollback.definition: Returning service to a previously validated model artifact.
rollback.explanation: Before activation, the chapter compares a candidate with the previous model on fixed canary inputs. A deviation beyond the declared tolerance selects the previous checkpoint. The local server then loads the selected file at startup. This makes rollback concrete and reversible, but it is not a live distributed swap: an operator must restart or reload the process and verify health. Production systems also coordinate traffic, compatibility, and database or feature changes.
